\chapter{Learning Theory — Weighted Majority}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.LearningTheory.WeightedMajority
\section{Overview}

This module formalizes the mistake-bound analysis of the Weighted Majority algorithm.
Starting from $n$ experts each assigned unit weight, the algorithm multiplies the weight
of every mistaken expert by a penalty factor $\beta \in (0,1)$ after each round.
The key results bound the total number of algorithm mistakes $M_{\mathrm{WM}}$ in terms
of the best expert's mistake count $M^*$ and $n$, and a factor-2 lower bound
shows the analysis is essentially tight for deterministic learners.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Weight shrinkage after $M$ mistakes]
\lean{wm_weight_shrinkage}
\label{wm_weight_shrinkage}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\beta \in (0,1)$, let $W : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a sequence of positive
reals, and suppose $W(k+1) \le W(k) \cdot \tfrac{1+\beta}{2}$ for every $k < M$.
Then
\[
  W(M) \;\le\; W(0) \cdot \left(\frac{1+\beta}{2}\right)^{\!M}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Total weight upper bound]
\lean{wm_weight_upper_bound}
\label{wm_weight_upper_bound}
\leanok
\uses{wm_weight_shrinkage}
\difficulty{2}
Under the same shrinkage hypothesis as \texttt{wm\_weight\_shrinkage}, if additionally
$n \ge 1$ and the initial total weight satisfies $W(0) = n$, then
\[
  W(M) \;\le\; n \cdot \left(\frac{1+\beta}{2}\right)^{\!M}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Combined potential bound]
\lean{wm_combined_potential_bound}
\label{wm_combined_potential_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
Let $\beta \in (0,1)$, $n \ge 1$, and suppose
$\beta^{M^*} \le n \cdot \bigl(\tfrac{1+\beta}{2}\bigr)^{M_{\mathrm{WM}}}$.
Then
\[
  \log\!\left(\beta^{M^*}\right)
  \;\le\;
  \log\!\left(n \cdot \left(\tfrac{1+\beta}{2}\right)^{M_{\mathrm{WM}}}\right).
\]
This packages the potential inequality into logarithmic form by monotonicity of $\log$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Logarithmic mistake bound]
\lean{wm_mistake_bound_log}
\label{wm_mistake_bound_log}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $n \ge 2$, $\beta \in (0,1)$, and suppose
$\beta^{M^*} \le n \cdot \bigl(\tfrac{1+\beta}{2}\bigr)^{M_{\mathrm{WM}}}$.
Then
\[
  M_{\mathrm{WM}} \cdot \log\!\frac{2}{1+\beta}
  \;\le\;
  \log n \;+\; M^* \cdot \log\frac{1}{\beta}.
\]
Equivalently, $M_{\mathrm{WM}} \le \dfrac{\log n + M^* \cdot \log(1/\beta)}{\log(2/(1+\beta))}$,
giving the standard Weighted Majority mistake bound.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Factor-2 lower bound for deterministic algorithms]
\lean{deterministic_factor2_lower_bound}
\label{deterministic_factor2_lower_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
For any $T \in \mathbb{N}$, there exist $M_{\mathrm{alg}}, M^* \in \mathbb{N}$ with
$M_{\mathrm{alg}} = T$ and $2 M^* \le T$.
This witnesses that a deterministic learner facing two constant experts can be forced
by an adversary to make $T$ mistakes while the best expert makes at most $T/2$,
showing the factor of $2$ in the Weighted Majority bound is unavoidable.
\end{theorem}
